note: SNG-252 §2b/§2c (Aevi 2026-08-01): the unified-ribbon copy - the connective strings CCode needs when it folds the whole engaged encounter into ONE enc-frame container. The flavor 'watch for' line becomes the ribbon SUBTITLE (not orphaned between panels); the moves get an in-ribbon header; the freeform line stays. Voice: spare, present-tense, the ribbon speaks the encounter as one object.

subtitle.note: the SNG-247 'watch for' flavor line, folded in UNDER the header as the ribbon's subtitle (was orphaned between the frame and the moves panel). Per-kind, short.

byKind.fight: a real fight — it can hurt you; the meter is blood
byKind.chase: wind and ground — losing costs breath, not blood; break contact to win
byKind.standoff: a contest of will — it cannot hurt you, however badly it goes; their resolve is the meter
byKind.puzzle: a sealed thing — understood, not beaten; win the read and a layer gives
byKind.hazard: hard ground — the fast one; a short brutal crossing, cross it before it costs you

movesHeader.note: the in-ribbon header for the moves section (replaces the separate panel's hint). Present when the ribbon is engaged.
movesHeader.text: Your moves — grouped by what they do. Or describe your own above; the {kind} rules bind either way.

freeform.note: CORRECTED (Aevi 2026-08-01): this is the FRAGMENT the frame WRAPS, not a whole line. The frame template renders: ▸ {cue} {wrapSuffix}. So `cue` is the bare freeform phrase and `wrapSuffix` is the moves pointer - the frame supplies the ▸. Previously `text` was a full self-contained line (its own ▸ + its own moves clause) that DOUBLED the frame's wrapper and still said 'Moves below' when moves are now IN the ribbon. Now it composes cleanly.
freeform.cue: describe your own move — the exits are shortcuts; the {kind} resolves whatever you try, against the stage
freeform.wrapSuffix: — or pick a grouped move above
freeform.shortcutNote: the moves are shortcuts to intent; a typed move routes through the same rules — never a cage
freeform.replaces: FRAME_FREEFORM_CUE (encounterFrame.js:334) + the '— or tap ⚙ Moves below' suffix in the app.js:8648 template. The moves moved INTO the ribbon (SNG-252), so the suffix points 'above', not 'below'.

wardDisabled.note: a move the encounter FORBIDS (SNG-230 §7b ward) reads disabled-with-reason IN the moves, not offered-then-refused.

collapse.note: the ⚙ still collapses the moves for space; default is SHOWN when engaged (Erik's intent).

howCCodeUses: When the ribbon is engaged (§2b), render as ONE enc-frame: header → subtitle (byKind) → win/meter/receipt → exits → movesHeader + the grouped moves (SNG-252 §2c, hints from encounter_move_hints.json) → freeform. The moves are open by default; ⚙ collapses. No separate moves-panel append - it's all inside the one container.

collapsedMoves.note: SNG-252b (Aevi): the COLLAPSED moves affordance - shown by default; the cards expand on tap. Summarizes what's available by family so the player knows what's there without the wall. CCode builds the count string from the owned-by-family tally.
collapsedMoves.summaryFormat: {n} {familyWord}, joined by ' · ' — e.g. '4 reads, 1 strike'; use the family's plain word (reveal→reads, strike→strikes, ward→guards, heal→mends, etc.)
collapsedMoves.empty: ⚙ No learned crafts to shortcut — describe your move below

turnDetail.note: SNG-252b: intensity + the Sense→Action→Bonus→Execute chain are ADVANCED controls; tuck them behind this toggle so they don't compete with the scene. Default hidden.
turnDetail.label: ⚙ turn detail
turnDetail.hint: intensity + the action chain — for fine control of the turn

hierarchy.note: SNG-252b: the ribbon render ORDER (importance top to bottom).
order: where you stand (win + meter + receipt, ONE compact row)
what you can do (⚙ moves collapsed + freeform line)

familyBlurbRule.note: SNG-252b §2d: the family-level blurb (e.g. 'reads THEM — sharpens the fog') shows ONCE as the family group header, NOT on every chip. Each move card shows only its OWN distinguishing line ('finds the opening, the trick' vs 'finds the pattern in how they fight'). Family blurb once per group; per-move line per move.
